summary.headline: JM Financial FY26 PAT rose 46% to INR1,202 crore (ROE 11.7%); Q4 segment profits weak as capital markets deals stalled amid FPI selling.
summary.overview: JM Financial's Q4 FY26 call framed FY26 as a strong year on a two-year pivot basis: reported PAT after minority rose 46% to INR1,202 crore, or INR1,133 crore excluding a one-off tax-refund interest gain and Labour Code impact, up 38%. Q4 was weak across capital markets, wealth and private markets because primary issuance stalled amid FPI selling and West Asia-related volatility. Management said the IPO pipeline (INR1.4 lakh crore across 55 filings) remains strong and expects the second half of FY27 to be better than the first. Guidance centred on Wealth Management productivity, Private Markets loan book growth of 15-20%, and Affordable Home Loans AUM growth of 25%.

financial_highlights.metric: Reported PAT after minority interest FY26
Operating PAT adjusted for one-offs FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR10,605 crore; book value about INR111/share

financial_highlights.metric: Dividend paid or proposed over last 4 quarters
financial_highlights.value: about INR5.95/share, about INR570 crore total

segments.name: Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets (CACM)
segments.commentary: FY26 net revenue about INR789 crore (+11%), operating PAT INR347 crore, capital employed INR829 crore (ROE about 47%). 41 capital markets deals worth about INR95,000 crore closed; Q4 segment PAT only INR39 crore due to lack of primary issuance.

segments.name: Private Markets
segments.commentary: FY26 operating PBT INR742 crore (3.5x) and PAT after minority INR543 crore (about 3.6x); capital employed about INR6,600 crore. Q4 segment profit after minority INR78 crore. Core loan book about INR4,000 crore, with distressed credit INR3,665 crore.

segments.name: Wealth Management
segments.commentary: Net revenue FY26 about INR775 crore (+9%), operating PAT INR132 crore, capital employed INR1,157 crore (ROE about 12%). Recurring AUM about INR31,000 crore (+10%), 29% of total; 1,046 RMs (+30%); 72 branches. Q4 segment profit INR39 crore.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: Mutual fund management fees FY26 about INR44 crore (+65%); average non-liquid MF AUM about INR10,500 crore. Segment loss after minority about INR30 crore in FY26 and INR5 crore in Q4. Employees 217 (+17%).

segments.name: Affordable Home Loans
segments.commentary: AUM about INR3,460 crore (+22%); FY26 revenue INR455 crore (+25%); operating PAT after minority INR74 crore (+45%); capital employed INR833 crore. Gross NPA 0.5%, collection efficiency 99.4% at March 2026; Q4 segment profit INR25 crore.

guidance_outlook: Wealth Management AUM growth of about 20% (up to 25%) in FY27; implied net inflows about INR6,000 crore; Wealth breakeven targeted in FY27 and better ROE in FY28-29, with long-term ROE of 15-18%.

Private Markets core loan book to grow 15-20% to about INR5,000 crore by March 2027; distressed credit assumed to grow about 15%; equity and alternatives capped at 20% of the roughly INR13,000 crore asset base.
Expected Private Markets recoveries of INR250-300 crore in FY27, matching FY28 target.
Affordable Home Loans AUM to grow 25% YoY; IPO targeted in FY28-29.
Asset Management expected to burn for about 2 more years; pre-IPO fund first close and total raise above INR1,000 crore, with a PE fund to follow.
Dividend payout of 50% of PAT committed; CACM business to double every 4-5 years on a peak-to-peak basis; long-term target of 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE.
capex_capacity: Wealth digital and BlinkX investment of about INR40-50 crore a year to be cut significantly within 3-6 months.
Wealth RM additions of about 80 in FY26; productivity gains expected over the next 3-6 months.
Affordable Home Loans branch network at 151 and customer base above 33,000; Bajaj Allianz bought 2.1% at a INR3,100 crore valuation (INR65 crore investment).
Margin trade finance book grew from INR300-400 crore to about INR2,000 crore.
Research coverage of about 400 stocks active and 150 soft coverage.
demand_pricing: IPO pipeline INR1.4 lakh crore (55 filings); management expects pipeline to roughly double YoY by Sept/Oct 2026, with some projections of INR2 lakh crore by October.
Management says it needs 7-8 months of visibility to push a large part of the pipeline; execution expected slow in Q1 FY27.
FPI ownership cited at about 15% versus a high of about 19%; domestic MFs described as conservative on IPO pricing.
Real estate lending risk-adjusted returns judged unattractive; growth expected to come from corporate and large-cap syndication.
Wealth transactional revenue expected to be about 50% of Wealth fees; broking less than 50% of that.

qa_highlights.question: Are IPO valuations being cut, and when will FPIs return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed FPI rotation to AI-led markets, oil near USD90-92 after elevated levels, and conservative domestic MF pricing; expects a 12-18 month window to open, with H2 FY27 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Can Private Markets drive revenue growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Loan book to grow 15-20% to about INR5,000 crore by March 2027; model shifting to fee-based syndication, with real estate growth slower given weak risk-adjusted returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CACM employee cost rise about INR100 crore while revenue rose about INR259 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipeline growth needs more people, derivatives business was built on the institutional equity platform, and research coverage was expanded deliberately as a tactical decision two years ago.

qa_highlights.question: What are the targets for Wealth Management and the Private Markets book?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth AUM growth about 20% (inflows about INR6,000 crore); Wealth breakeven in FY27; long-term ROE 15-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is a segment demerger possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is possible but businesses must scale first; listing or liquidity options for units may come in one to two years.

risks_watch: Continued FPI selling and West Asia/oil-driven volatility could keep the IPO and QIP pipeline stalled into Q1 FY27.
Q4 CACM profit fell to INR39 crore; CACM and Private Markets earnings are lumpy and need peak-to-peak assessment.
Wealth ROE is about 12% and Asset Management is still loss-making; margin expansion and productivity gains need to show in FY27.
Private Markets write-backs flatter FY26 profit; sustained profits depend on loan growth and syndication fees.
Rising interest rates could affect the fixed-income syndication outlook.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term pipeline and strategy, but cautious near term: management acknowledged Q4 and Q1 FY27 slowdown in capital markets and repeatedly guided to H2 FY27 recovery. Evasive on Wealth margin breakdown (declined to split PBT between recurring and transactional revenue).
key_quotes: We need a clear 7 to 8 months visibility of the year to be able to push a large part of the pipeline through.
Private Markets will see good amount of loan book growth this year as well as I expect, as I said, around INR250 crores to INR300 crores of further recovery.
We are committed to declaring 50% of that PAT as dividend every year for our shareholders.
We don't want to be at more than a certain debt equity ratio in the private market space of more than 2:1 or 3:1.

adds.what: Wealth Management RM additions (about 80 RMs added in FY26; 1,046 RMs total, +30%)
Affordable Home Loans branch network at 151 branches (existing, no new branch count given)

growth.why: Management guides Wealth AUM growth of about 20-25% in FY27 (implied net inflows about INR6,000 crore), Private Markets core loan book +15-20% to about INR5,000 crore, and Affordable Home Loans AUM +25%, backed by RM additions and IPO pipeline visibility but no specific new capacity or order numbers; Q4 segment profits were weak.
